verdicts.what_changed: Confirmed first in the worktree: the new per-frame test recorded the uppercut as IF IF - - (the flash only under the impact frame). Fix at the root: CombatActor.impact_frame_ticks(hit) (static) returns Tuning.vfx_impact_frame_frames for a clean FINISHER hit with impact_frame_enabled, else 0. It is decided from the hit's tier and the tunables, the way VfxDirector decides, and never reads VfxDirector. receive_hit passes it to _flash_at(..., delay). The flash is aimed on the struck part at the hit tick (HumanoidRig.flash_at(..., color, shown = false), so it is anchored on the bone as hit) but held hidden. _physics_process counts the wait in real ticks, skipping the start tick like the flash count does, then calls the new HumanoidRig.show_flash(), which draws the flash and follows the drawn bone. It then shows for exactly hit_flash_frames rendered frames. Clearing paths are unchanged: set_flash(0.0) clears the aimed flash, and reset_state and _vanish zero _flash_frames, which gates the wait. The parry _flash() resets the delay. The flash is not lengthened, and blocked hits, guard breaks, light and heavy hits and toggle-off hits are unchanged. ARCHITECTURE's Hit flash 'Frames' bullet has one sentence on the delay.
verdicts.tests: tests/test_hit_flash.gd: test_a_finisher_flashes_right_after_its_impact_frame runs a real P P P P with a VfxDirector added and records the impact frame and the flash per rendered frame. Cases [toggle on, 2, 2], [on, 1, 3], [on, 0, 2] and [off, 2, 2] give the uppercut I I F F - ... with the toggle on and F F - ... with it off or at 0 frames; the jabs and the hook flash from their hit frames. It runs through the real hitstop and slow-mo. The first two cases failed before the fix. test_a_finisher_s_late_flash_lands_on_the_struck_part_and_a_ko_still_flashes: a KO launch finisher shows I I F F - -, with no overlay at the hit, and lands at full strength on the drawn head of the ragdolled body; a reset_state() during the wait cancels the flash. test_p_p_p_p_flashes_each_struck_part_as_drawn now measures the uppercut on the first frame its flash shows. 13/13 in the file; full suite 486/486, no SCRIPT ERROR or ERROR.

captures.description: vfx_bot 'VFX: P P P P' after the fix: first person (uppercut at f70, video 69-70 impact frame), side view (f227) and impact frame off (f383). Log: pppp.log.

The same acts with --tune=hit_flash_strength=0, as a pixel-diff reference. Diffs: first person changes only on video 71-72 (1.7-2.0% of the screen, brighter, on the chin and neck), exactly after the impact frame at 69-70. Impact frame off changes only on 382-383 (1.5-1.8%). Side view with effects on changes nothing at 228-229 (the burst and KRAK cover it: hit-05).
First person, video 66-77 at 60 stills per second: impact frame on tiles 4-5 (69-70), the flash on the struck chin and neck on tiles 6-7 (71-72).
Close crop: first-person frames 71 and 72 with the flash, beside frame 71 without it.
Side view, video 224-231: impact frame 226-227, then the large burst and KRAK over the struck head and chest.

Side view with vfx_scale 0 (capture only; side_novfx.avi against side_novfx_noflash.avi), video 68-72: the impact frame at 69-70, then the white flash on the launched dummy's chin and upper chest on exactly 71-72 (the diff changes only those two frames).
Impact frame off, video 379-390: the flash on the uppercut's own frames 382-383, unchanged.

feel_judgement: In first person the finisher now has a second beat: the ink impact frame for 2 frames, then a white bloom on the struck chin and neck around the fist for 2 frames. It matches the flash's size and look with the impact frame off (about 2% of the screen against 1.5-1.8%), so it reads as the same flash, just after the frame. It doesn't feel late or stretched, because the 2-frame count is kept. In side view the delayed flash runs correctly: with the effects off, a bright white patch shows on the launched body's chin and chest on exactly the 2 frames after the impact frame. With the effects on, the large finisher burst and KRAK fully cover it (0 pixels change), as they cover every side-view flash. That is hit-05 and the side-view flash question still open with Game-boy; burst sizes were not changed.
remaining: Side view: the finisher's delayed flash is still fully hidden under the large burst and its word. That belongs to hit-05 (the view-share floor's burst sizes) and the open side-view flash question with Game-boy; it was left untouched.

Edge case not addressed (out of scope, not seen in play): a different victim's light or heavy hit landing within the 2 frames of another finisher's impact frame would still have its flash under that frame, since the delay is decided per hit.
No tunables were added, so tuning/default.json needs no regeneration for this branch.
